**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the token diagnosis qualified**

This summary still states as fact that Cursor's minted token lacks the `issues` scope, even though the revised evidence section at lines 78–83 now explicitly says neither the token nor installation settings were inspected and the project's root cause remains unconfirmed. That fresh qualification directly contradicts this remaining categorical instance and may lead the owner to deploy a broad PAT instead of investigating another integration or proxy restriction; describe the missing scope as the externally reported explanation rather than an established project fact.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Leave untested settings lanes as unknown**

This attributes repository-settings refusals to every provider, but the capability table immediately below records settings access as `not recorded` for Cursor user mode and xAI/Grok, while the Cloud Agent cell supplies no refusal status despite the stated meaning of “no.” Where one of those authentication paths is settings-capable, this overclaim unnecessarily leaves the ruleset change as an owner-only action and contradicts the document's own requirement that uninspected operations remain UNKNOWN; limit the statement to the OpenAI and Claude refusals actually recorded.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Separate the unobserved PR operations**

This marks the combined “PR comments, reviews, merge” capability as yes for Cursor Cloud Agents, but the cited `merged_by` fields establish only that `cursor[bot]` performed merges; they do not show that the installation token can post PR comments or submit reviews. Those endpoints can require different permissions—exactly the distinction exposed by the issue-comment failures in this same row—so split these operations or leave comments and reviews UNKNOWN rather than treating merge evidence as proof of all three.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep cross-repository reads marked unverified**

When Cursor continues minting a token scoped to the task repository—as this record says it currently does—adding repositories to the app installation does not by itself make those repositories readable: GitHub [documents](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app) that an installation token can remain restricted to a subset of the installation's repositories. The claim that this action makes reads “resolve everywhere” therefore overstates an untested outcome; leave cross-repository reads unknown and require a readback, or state that Cursor must widen the minted token as well.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Account for the single-parent first-parent commit**

Fresh repository evidence beyond the earlier bypass concern contradicts this remaining topology claim: `git log --first-parent` on the target's ancestry includes the 2 October commit `9677f2849994f794f3956beec86e6ba7158c0306`, and its commit object has only the single parent `97840180d889869ce1b5f0d61a163d957918a524`. It therefore cannot be a merge commit or have a tree equal to a mechanical merge of its parents; classify this squash/direct update and inspect its associated PR, checks, and ruleset evidence instead of asserting that every first-parent commit has merge topology.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark post-installation write scope as unknown**

When action 4 adds all project repositories to the Cursor installation, cross-repository writes may become available without Cursor changing how it mints tokens: [GitHub documents](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app) that omitting `repositories`/`repository_ids` gives a token access to every repository granted to the installation. The current task-repository-only observation cannot distinguish an explicitly restricted token from an installation that currently includes only that repository, so writes—like reads—must remain UNKNOWN until tested; otherwise the owner may underestimate the widened credential's write scope.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin the installation token in the scope probe**

When actions 1 and 4 are performed together and this cross-repository comment is attempted through `gh`, the result cannot establish the installation token's scope: the [GitHub CLI documentation](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_environment) says that `GH_TOKEN` takes precedence over stored credentials, and action 1 supplies that PAT with access to all four repositories. A successful comment could therefore be entirely PAT-authenticated even though this sentence says it observes the widened installation's write scope; require the probe to pin and report the authentication path (likewise for the read probe), or keep installation-token access UNKNOWN.

The correction mentions only the pull-request and check exemptions, and “The sentence before this one” grammatically marks the live correction—not the older repository-admin claim—as superseded. This is fresh final-state evidence beyond the earlier thread: explicitly qualify the force-push/deletion claims for non-bypass actors and identify the old snapshot unambiguously.

**ACCESS-HANDOFF-01 (P2): reconcile the operational handoff branch with the general no-rerouting rule.** This bullet gives a default handoff after attach/credential-read refusal, but stops handoff explicitly only for a specific write with additional no-other-route wording. The cited C02 receipt6042173762 records an attach classifier denial and an explicit stop. Classify the exact restriction before any relay; a denial must not become permission merely because the extra phrase is absent or a different operation exposed it. Preserve legitimate missing-tool handoffs where neither action nor handoff is prohibited, and keep unrelated authorized work moving. See the parent review's five semantic controls.

**ACCESS-HANDOFF-02 (P2): keep the sample as attributed observations, not a general mechanism or publishing forecast.** The two cited answers show different attach outcomes across sessions/repository arguments; C01 expressly limited its report and did not inspect credentials. They do not establish a general cause for credential-read/write refusals or support the later 'another Claude session usually can' prediction. Preserve the receipts, qualify the per-call interpretation as reported, and leave cause/retryability/future capabilities unestablished. No new capability probes or census are requested.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Qualify the remaining Cursor diagnosis**

After the earlier diagnosis correction, this sentence still identifies Cursor's limitation as the explanation and explicitly rules out an installation setting, even though lines 104–109 say that neither this installation nor its minted token was inspected and that another integration or proxy restriction remains possible. If this project's permissions differ from the forum reports, the categorical wording can send the owner toward a broad PAT without establishing the cause; present the limitation as a hypothesis instead. Fresh final-state evidence beyond the earlier finding is the retained unconfirmed-root-cause qualification in lines 104–109.

C162-ACCESS-01 / P2 (residual4211146234): absent Issues write identifies a configuration obstacle, not necessarily the layer that caused a recorded refusal. Two compatible histories are (a) GitHub rejects for that missing permission and (b) a proxy denies first while the permission deficit also exists. The source retains that proxy/token uncertainty, so the page alone cannot choose between them. Similarly, present Issues write rules out only that specific permission deficit at the inspected installation/time, not all installation/repository-access causes. Smallest amendment: state those bounded observations and leave causal attribution UNKNOWN without suitably scoped evidence. Full counterexamples and proposed paragraph in C162 report; no credential probe needed.

This still asserts that all recorded refusals come from three identified sources, although the Cursor bullet immediately says the project token was not inspected and that the failure could instead originate in the installation configuration, while lines 107–114 also retain another integration or proxy restriction as possible. In an installation that lacks Issues write, this categorical summary misstates the evidence and can prematurely direct the owner to the PAT workaround; describe these as candidate sources and keep only the observed refusals confirmed. The fresh final-state evidence beyond the earlier diagnosis comments is the explicit `UNKNOWN` qualification at lines 47–50.
